+<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\theta,\Pi}(y|x)=\frac{1}{|\Pi|}\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}p_{\theta}(y|\Gamma_{\pi}(x))" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\theta,\Pi}(y|x)=\frac{1}{|\Pi|}\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}p_{\theta}(y|\Gamma_{\pi}(x))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
+</table>
+<p id="Thmtheorem3.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem3.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If the model class includes such tied-weight multi-branch compositions with a linear averaging head, it is closed under finite permutation mixtures. As <math id="Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\Pi|\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\Pi|\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> along i.i.d. draws from the uniform measure over permutations, <math id="Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\theta,\Pi}\Rightarrow\bar{p}_{\theta}(y|x)=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[p_{\theta}(y|\Gamma_{\pi}(x))]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\theta,\Pi}\Rightarrow\bar{p}_{\theta}(y|x)=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[p_{\theta}(y|\Gamma_{\pi}(x))]</annotation></semantics></math> almost surely.</span></p>
+</div>
+</div>
+<div id="S3.SS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
+<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
+<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">The only operation beyond the base model is a convex combination in probability space. Since each branch outputs a normalized distribution, the average is also a normalized distribution and is implementable by a fixed linear layer that sums corresponding probabilities across branches with weights <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/|\Pi|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/|\Pi|</annotation></semantics></math>. Tied weights ensure the branches are copies of <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> evaluated at permuted inputs, so the composite realizes the desired mixture. By the strong law of large numbers, the empirical average over i.i.d. permutations converges pointwise to the permutation expectation.
+∎</span></p>
+</div>
+</div>

+<div id="S3.SS3.3" class="ltx_proof">
+<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
+<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">The risk decomposition follows from the chain rule for KL divergence. Since Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3 (Permutation-mixture realizability with averaging head). ‣ 3.3 MDL Optimality Through Architectural Closure ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> guarantees the model family contains <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{p}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{p}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, the convex hull of permutation mixtures is realizable. The I-projection of <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="P(\cdot|T(X))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(\cdot|T(X))</annotation></semantics></math> onto this convex hull minimizes the KL divergence, and when the target is realizable (i.e., exchangeable and in the convex hull), the residual term vanishes, yielding MDL optimality in expectation.
+∎</span></p>
+</div>

+</section>
+<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>The Expectation-level Decompression Law</h3>
+
+<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Binary adjudication is the natural unit of analysis as EDFL provides closed-form bounds for Bernoulli events and production systems make binary answer/abstain decisions (we evaluate via Bernoulli predicates <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, details in Appendix B).</p>
+</div>
+<div id="Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
+<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 5</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Expectation-level Decompression Law (EDFL))<span id="Thmtheorem5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
+<div id="Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any event <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> with prior mass <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{q}=\bar{S}(\mathcal{A})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>S</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{q}=\bar{S}(\mathcal{A})</annotation></semantics></math> and posterior mass <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=P(\mathcal{A})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=P(\mathcal{A})</annotation></semantics></math>, the expected information budget satisfies:</span></p>
+<table id="S3.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">
+
+<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\bar{\Delta}:=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[\operatorname{KL}(P\|S_{\pi})]\geq\operatorname{KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(p)\|\operatorname{Ber}(\bar{q}))" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>:=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Ber</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>Ber</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\Delta}:=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[\operatorname{KL}(P\|S_{\pi})]\geq\operatorname{KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(p)\|\operatorname{Ber}(\bar{q}))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
+</table>
+<p id="Thmtheorem5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">with equality when <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math>-projection of <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>S</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{S}</annotation></semantics></math> onto <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{Q:Q(\mathcal{A})=p\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{Q:Q(\mathcal{A})=p\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Equality holds for the exponentially tilted distribution <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{\star}(y)\propto\bar{S}(y)e^{\lambda g(y)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>S</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{\star}(y)\propto\bar{S}(y)e^{\lambda g(y)}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> chosen so <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{\star}(\mathcal{A})=p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{\star}(\mathcal{A})=p</annotation></semantics></math> (standard <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math>-projection).</span></p>
+</div>
+</div>

+<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmcorollary1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 1</span></span><span id="Thmcorollary1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Compression Failure for Rare Events)<span id="Thmcorollary1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>

+<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5 </span>Operational Planners</h3>
+
+<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_minipage ltx_align_center" style="width:207.0pt;">
+<span id="S3.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_middle ltx_framed ltx_framed_rectangle" style="width:196.7pt;">
+<span id="S3.SS5.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Box 1: Hallucination Prevention Metrics
+<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:2.0pt;"></span></span>
+<span id="S3.I2" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
+<span id="S3.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
+<span id="S3.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
+<span id="S3.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\text{B2T}(x;h^{*})=\operatorname{KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(1-h^{*})\|\operatorname{Ber}(q_{\text{lo}}(x)))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>B2T</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Ber</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>Ber</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mtext>lo</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{B2T}(x;h^{*})=\operatorname{KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(1-h^{*})\|\operatorname{Ber}(q_{\text{lo}}(x)))</annotation></semantics></math></span>
+</span></span>
+<span id="S3.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
+<span id="S3.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
+<span id="S3.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{RoH}(x)=1-p_{\max}(\bar{\Delta}(x),\bar{q}(x))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>RoH</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{RoH}(x)=1-p_{\max}(\bar{\Delta}(x),\bar{q}(x))</annotation></semantics></math></span>
+</span></span>
+<span id="S3.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
+<span id="S3.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<span id="S3.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{ISR}(x)=\bar{\Delta}(x)/\operatorname{B2T}(x;h^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>ISR</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>B2T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{ISR}(x)=\bar{\Delta}(x)/\operatorname{B2T}(x;h^{*})</annotation></semantics></math></span>
+</span></span>
+</span>
+<span id="S3.SS5.p1.1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p1.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Decision rule:</span> ISR &lt; 1 → abstain; ISR <math id="S3.SS5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> → answer</span>
+</span></p>
+</div>
+<div id="S3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">From EDFL, the abstain/answer rule uses a fixed ISR threshold of 1.0 determined analytically. Evidence permutations, clipping (<math id="S3.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B{=}6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B{=}6</annotation></semantics></math>), and seeds were set before scoring, ensuring boundary alignment is a falsifiable out-of-sample check. B2T, RoH, and ISR are derived from EDFL as operational planners for deployment-time decisions.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S3.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S3.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p ltx_minipage ltx_align_center" style="width:269.1pt;">
+<span id="S3.SS5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_middle ltx_framed ltx_framed_rectangle" style="width:255.6pt;">

Compute B2T for several conservative priors <math id="S3.SS5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\text{lo}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mtext>lo</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\text{lo}}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span>

+<span id="S3.SS5.p3.1.1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p3.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Budget <math id="S3.SS5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\Delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\Delta}</annotation></semantics></math> to reliability.</span> Given <math id="S3.SS5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{q}=0.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{q}=0.10</annotation></semantics></math>, the maximum achievable success at budget <math id="S3.SS5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\Delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\Delta}</annotation></semantics></math> solves <math id="S3.SS5.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{KL}(\mathrm{Ber}(p)\,\|\,\mathrm{Ber}(0.10))\leq\bar{\Delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Ber</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><mi>Ber</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KL}(\mathrm{Ber}(p)\,\|\,\mathrm{Ber}(0.10))\leq\bar{\Delta}</annotation></semantics></math>. +<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
+<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{array}[]{c|cccc}\bar{\Delta}\ (\text{nats})&amp;0.5&amp;1.0&amp;2.0&amp;3.0\\
+\hline\cr p_{\max}&amp;0.495&amp;0.689&amp;0.951&amp;\approx 1.000\end{array}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_border_r"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>nats</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd><mtd><mn>0.5</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>1.0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>2.0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>3.0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_border_t"></mtd><mtd class="ltx_border_t"></mtd><mtd class="ltx_border_t"></mtd><mtd class="ltx_border_t"></mtd><mtd class="ltx_border_t"></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_border_r"><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mtd><mtd><mn>0.495</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>0.689</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>0.951</mn></mtd><mtd><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.000</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{array}[]{c|cccc}\bar{\Delta}\ (\text{nats})&amp;0.5&amp;1.0&amp;2.0&amp;3.0\\
+\hline\cr p_{\max}&amp;0.495&amp;0.689&amp;0.951&amp;\approx 1.000\end{array}</annotation></semantics></math></span>
+<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
+</span>
+<span id="S3.SS5.p3.1.1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p3.1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ISR gate.</span> If <math id="S3.SS5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{q}=0.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{q}=0.10</annotation></semantics></math> and measured <math id="S3.SS5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\Delta}=2.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>2.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\Delta}=2.0</annotation></semantics></math>, then
+<math id="S3.SS5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ISR}=\bar{\Delta}/\mathrm{B2T}=2.0/1.994\approx 1.00\Rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ISR</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>/</mo><mi>B2T</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2.0</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>1.994</mn></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.00</mn><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ISR}=\bar{\Delta}/\mathrm{B2T}=2.0/1.994\approx 1.00\Rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS5.p3.1.1.4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">answer.</span>
+If instead <math id="S3.SS5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\text{lo}}=0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mtext>lo</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.02</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\text{lo}}=0.02</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S3.SS5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{B2T}=3.519" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B2T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3.519</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{B2T}=3.519</annotation></semantics></math> and the same budget gives
+<math id="S3.SS5.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ISR}\approx 0.57\Rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ISR</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.57</mn><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ISR}\approx 0.57\Rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS5.p3.1.1.4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">abstain or acquire info</span>.</span>
+</span></p>

+<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
+<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments</h2>
+
+<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Experimental setup.</span> We use our custom-built Factuality Slice dataset comprising 3,059 evidence-grounded QA items from FEVER, HotpotQA, NQ-Open, and PopQA with controlled evidence chunks and hard negatives (see Appendix H for complete documentation). All prompts, scoring code, and fixed seeds used in this paper are documented in Appendix H to permit exact replication without hyperparameter tuning.</p>
+</div>
+<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Experiment 1: MDL Optimality via Permutation Mixtures</h3>
+
+<section id="S4.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
+<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.1.1 </span>Ground-Truth Validation</h4>
+
+<section id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
+<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Design.</h5>
+
+<div id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct large-scale dispersion studies on 3,059 binary classification items from all splits spanning <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[3,60]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[3,60]</annotation></semantics></math> chunks (58 distinct <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> values). Each item contains 48-token-capped evidence chunks with binary gold labels. We test Qwen2-7B-Instruct (m=12 unique banded permutations) and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (m=16 unique banded permutations), both with 4-bit NF4 quantization. We draw unique banded permutations (6 bands, shuffle within), compute predictions <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext='q_{\pi}(x)=P_{\pi}(\text{"1"})/(P_{\pi}(\text{"1"})+P_{\pi}(\text{"0"}))' display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>"1"</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>"1"</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>"0"</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\pi}(x)=P_{\pi}(\text{"1"})/(P_{\pi}(\text{"1"})+P_{\pi}(\text{"0"}))</annotation></semantics></math> via renormalized label token probabilities, and form uniform mixture <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{q}(x)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{k=1}^{m}q_{\pi_{k}}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>m</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation +</div>
+</section>

+<p id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Mean absolute residual <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|R_{\pi}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|R_{\pi}|</annotation></semantics></math> follows <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a+b\ln n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a+b\ln n</annotation></semantics></math> across both models, confirming Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Quantified Martingale Violation). ‣ 3.2 Quantified Martingale Violations ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. +<section id="S4.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
+<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.1.2 </span>Self-Consistency Analysis</h4>
+
+<div id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We fix a canonical continuation <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> once per item (chosen from the identity ordering by argmax over the two label probabilities), score that same <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> under <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=16</annotation></semantics></math> banded permutations of the evidence (<math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[3,60]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[3,60]</annotation></semantics></math>), and compare single-permutation vs. mixture behavior. For each item we compute the Jensen gap</p>
+<table id="S4.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">
+
+<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{k}[-\log S_{k}(Y)]}_{\text{mean single-perm CE}}\;-\;\underbrace{-\log\mathbb{E}_{k}[S_{k}(Y)]}_{\text{uniform mixture CE}}\;\geq 0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>mean single-perm CE</mtext></munder><mo lspace="0.502em" rspace="0.502em">−</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>uniform mixture CE</mtext></munder></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{k}[-\log S_{k}(Y)]}_{\text{mean single-perm CE}}\;-\;\underbrace{-\log\mathbb{E}_{k}[S_{k}(Y)]}_{\text{uniform mixture CE}}\;\geq 0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
+</table>
+<p id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(Y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(Y)</annotation></semantics></math> is the model’s probability of <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> under permutation <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> (two-label normalization). We also learn a global convex mixture over permutations (shared weights per <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>) by exponentiated-gradient and report its cross-entropy.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
+<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
+<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
+<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Qwen-2-7B-Instruct (3,059 items; <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=16</annotation></semantics></math>; <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[3,60]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[3,60]</annotation></semantics></math>).</span> Mean Jensen gap = 0.1041 nats/token (uniform mixture strictly improves over single permutations). The uniform mixture is essentially optimal: the mixture-optimality gap (uniform vs. globally optimized mixture) is <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> nats/token. The mean per-<math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> Jensen gaps are positive across the entire range <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=3\ldots 60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=3\ldots 60</annotation></semantics></math> (Appendix C).</p>
+</div></li>
+<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
+<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (same setup).</span> Mean Jensen gap = 0.00982 nats/token; the mixture-optimality gap is <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 5.3\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>5.3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 5.3\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> nats/token. Again, means are positive for every <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
+</div></li>
+</ul>
+</div>
+<div id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Together these results confirm the Jensen inequality at the item level (positive gaps) and show that uniform permutation mixtures achieve virtually the same cross-entropy as the globally optimized mixture, i.e., near-MDL optimality within the permutation family. (All numbers are in nats/token; full per-<math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> tables and weight vectors appear in Appendix C.)</p>
+</div>
+</section>
+</section>
+<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Experiment 2: Causal Dose-Response Analysis</h3>
+
+<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To establish causality, we conducted randomized experiments controlling information content while holding prompt length constant at L=4 chunks. We vary the dose <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\in\{0,1,2,3\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\in\{0,1,2,3\}</annotation></semantics></math> of support chunks versus non-support chunks.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Answer rate increases by 37.5 percentage points (pp), accuracy by 45.6pp, and hallucination decreases by 17.6pp from dose 0 to 3. <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\Delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\Delta}</annotation></semantics></math> increases at 0.375 nats per dose (Spearman <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=0.80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.80</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=0.80</annotation></semantics></math>, p&lt;0.001). The critical threshold where accuracy exceeds hallucination occurs at dose approximately equal to 1. Using random within-band order as exogenous variation, OLS slope of 0.127 fewer hallucinations per nat establishes information insufficiency as causal mechanism. The Llama-3.1-8B validation yields <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\approx 0.110" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.110</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\approx 0.110</annotation></semantics></math> hallucination reduction per nat (IV robustness in Appendix D). We use symmetric clipping for stability in the main experiments; min-clipping provides a provable lower-bound (Appendix A.5).</p>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Experiment 3: Pre-specified audit (deployment calibration)</h3>
+
+<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate on Gemma-2-9B fine-tuned on FEVER, HotpotQA, NQ-Open, and PopQA with 528 held-out items. Pre-specified settings: evidence permutations with seeds <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0,1,\ldots,5\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0,1,\ldots,5\}</annotation></semantics></math>, symmetric clipping at B=6 nats, preservation of role markers. Information budget: <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\Delta}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{k=1}^{m}\operatorname{clip}(\log P(y)-\log S_{k}(y),B)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>m</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>clip</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\Delta}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{k=1}^{m}\operatorname{clip}(\log P(y)-\log S_{k}(y),B)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Results: 96.2% boundary alignment [94.3, 97.5], near-0% hallucination [0.0, 0.7], 24.1% abstention [20.6, 27.9], 80.5% accuracy on attempts [76.8, 83.8]. Mean Jensen Gap <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathfrak{J}}_{\Gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔍</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathfrak{J}}_{\Gamma}</annotation></semantics></math> = 0.82 nats [0.71, 0.93]. Parameter sensitivity (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\in{3,6,12}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\in{3,6,12}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B\in{4,6,8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>∈</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B\in{4,6,8}</annotation></semantics></math>) shows robust alignment (details in Appendix E). Permutation skeleton ablations show that slopes vary from 0.245 (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\text{bands}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>K</mi><mtext>bands</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\text{bands}}</annotation></semantics></math>=3) to 0.291 (uniform permutations), with our 6-band configuration yielding intermediate values.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For rare events with low prior mass: <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{q}=0.000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{q}=0.000</annotation></semantics></math> requires 5.29 nats (ISR=0.16→Refuse); <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{q}=0.167" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.167</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{q}=0.167</annotation></semantics></math> requires 2.48 nats (ISR=1.06→Answer). Models achieve near-0% hallucination through calibrated refusal rather than random guessing. We find <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=3</annotation></semantics></math> captures most of the Jensen gain with 3× model calls; escalate to <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=6</annotation></semantics></math> only when ISR&lt;1 for critical decisions. This latency-reliability tradeoff enables practical deployment with controlled computational overhead.</p>
+</div>
+</section>
+</section>
+<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
+<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Synthesis</h2>
+
+<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The three experiments provide complementary validation, each mapping directly to our theoretical contributions. Experiment 1 validates Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Quantified Martingale Violation). ‣ 3.2 Quantified Martingale Violations ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> (QMV) through observed <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\log n)</annotation></semantics></math> scaling and Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 4 (MDL Optimality in Expectation). ‣ 3.3 MDL Optimality Through Architectural Closure ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> (MDL optimality) through strictly positive Jensen gaps. Experiment 2 validates Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 5 (Expectation-level Decompression Law (EDFL)). ‣ 3.4 The Expectation-level Decompression Law ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> (EDFL) by showing causal dose-response of hallucination to information budgets. Experiment 3 demonstrates the operational planners derived from EDFL work in practice with ISR=1.0 cleanly separating safe answering from abstention.</p>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
+<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Discussion</h2>
+
+<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Theoretical Implications</h3>
+
+<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our framework resolves the fundamental paradox through the key insight that positional encodings induce minimization of <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[\ell(Y|\Gamma_{\pi}(X))]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[\ell(Y|\Gamma_{\pi}(X))]</annotation></semantics></math> rather than <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(Y|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(Y|X)</annotation></semantics></math>, which admits a Kolmogorov-complexity interpretation up to additive constants. The theoretical results are modular and architecture-agnostic:</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1. Local stability suffices for logarithmic scaling.</span> The adjacent-swap stability assumption (Assumption <a href="#Thmassumption1" title="Assumption 1 (Local rank stability with bounded total variation). ‣ 3.2 Quantified Martingale Violations ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) is satisfied by a broad class of positional encodings (RoPE, ALiBi, learned) because LayerNorm, bounded Q/K norms, and softmax Lipschitz naturally imply small changes under adjacent swaps. Our bound controls an average-over-permutations quantity in the logit; it is complementary to analyses that consider worst-case positional deviations.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2. Assumption-free certificates provide safety guarantees.</span> The JS-based bound (Proposition <a href="#Thmproposition2" title="Proposition 2 (Assumption-free JS certificate). ‣ 3.2 Quantified Martingale Violations ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) requires no structural assumptions and can be computed directly from model outputs, providing per-item safety certificates.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S6.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S6.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3. Hallucinations are predictable compression failures.</span> Rather than stochastic errors, hallucinations arise deterministically when information budgets fall below EDFL thresholds.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S6.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S6.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">4. Calibrated abstention emerges from information-theoretic principles.</span> Models naturally refuse when ISR &lt; 1, suggesting safe behavior emerges from proper information management.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S6.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S6.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Our goal is a normative, information-theoretic account with deployable planners. The empirical sections are illustrative checks of the theory’s key predictions (dispersion scaling, mixture gains, and dose-response), not a benchmark study. We therefore do not add detector baselines or coverage-risk curves; these evaluate a different objective (post-hoc detection performance) than the ex-ante budgeting question we target. We release derivations and implementation details so that future work can plug EDFL/ISR into any evaluation suite.</p>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Practical Applications</h3>
+
+<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our operational planners enable: pre-generation risk assessment via ISR calculation; graduated responses using ISR thresholds (ISR &lt; 0.5: refuse, 0.5 to 1.0: hedge, &gt;1.0: answer); information acquisition when ISR &lt; 1; and ensemble robustness with <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\geq 6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\geq 6</annotation></semantics></math> permutations. The ground-truth experiments demonstrate permutation averaging provides practical benefits with reasonable computational overhead.</p>
+</div>
+<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A practical training-time regularizer directly targets the positional Jensen penalty: <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}+\lambda\mathbb{E}_{x}\mathbb{E}_{\pi,\pi^{\prime}}\left[(\operatorname{logit}q_{\pi}(x)-\operatorname{logit}q_{\pi^{\prime}}(x))^{2}\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>logit</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>π</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>logit</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}+\lambda\mathbb{E}_{x}\mathbb{E}_{\pi,\pi^{\prime}}\left[(\operatorname{logit}q_{\pi}(x)-\operatorname{logit}q_{\pi^{\prime}}(x))^{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>, shrinking prediction variance across permutations without changing the core architecture. This approach complements our inference-time methods.</p>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>Limitations</h3>
+
+<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We restrict evaluation to binary adjudication because EDFL’s guarantees are tightest for Bernoulli events. While EDFL extends to multi-class via one-vs-rest, the theory is sharpest for Bernoulli predicates that govern abstain/answer decisions in deployment. We therefore focus on Bernoulli adjudication and leave comprehensive multi-class evaluations to follow-on work. For structured outputs (code generation, reasoning chains), compositional predicates like unit tests or rubric satisfaction provide natural binary signals. The relationship between model scale and positional bias (Qwen2 vs Llama variation) deserves systematic investigation across architectures.</p>
+</div>
+</section>
+</section>
+<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
+<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>
+
+<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented a unified theory showing hallucinations are compression failures triggered by insufficient information for rare events. Our framework reconciles the paradox: transformers are “Bayesian in expectation, not in realization” due to positional processing. The QMV theorem provides explicit <math id="S7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\log n)</annotation></semantics></math> bounds, EDFL transforms hallucination to quantifiable risk, and operational planners enable prediction and prevention through principled information budgeting. The architectural closure theorem (Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3 (Permutation-mixture realizability with averaging head). ‣ 3.3 MDL Optimality Through Architectural Closure ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) shows these theoretical benefits are achievable in practice through ensemble architectures with averaging heads.</p>
+</div>
+</section>

+<p id="Thmlemma1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(t)=1/(1+e^{-t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(t)=1/(1+e^{-t})</annotation></semantics></math> and let <math id="Thmlemma1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q=\sigma(u)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q=\sigma(u)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmlemma1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\prime}=\sigma(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\prime}=\sigma(v)</annotation></semantics></math>. +<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">By the mean value theorem, <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\sigma(u)-\sigma(v)|=|\sigma^{\prime}(\xi)||u-v|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\sigma(u)-\sigma(v)|=|\sigma^{\prime}(\xi)||u-v|</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ξ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi</annotation></semantics></math> between <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{\prime}(t)=\sigma(t)(1-\sigma(t))\leq 1/4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{\prime}(t)=\sigma(t)(1-\sigma(t))\leq 1/4</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the result follows.

+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>A.2 Proof of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2 (Quantified Martingale Violation). ‣ 3.2 Quantified Martingale Violations ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> (Quantified Martingale Violation)</h3>
+
+<div id="A1.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
+<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2 (Quantified Martingale Violation). ‣ 3.2 Quantified Martingale Violations ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</h6>
+<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Write <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\pi}(x)=\sigma\!\big(a(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_{i}\psi(\mathrm{pos}_{\pi}(i))\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.437em;" width="0.437em"><mi>σ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>pos</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\pi}(x)=\sigma\!\big(a(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_{i}\psi(\mathrm{pos}_{\pi}(i))\big)</annotation></semantics></math> under Assumption <a href="#Thmassumption2" title="Assumption 2 (First-order positional sensitivity). ‣ 3.2 Quantified Martingale Violations ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. For i.i.d. permutations <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi,\pi^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi,\pi^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, by symmetrization,</span></p>
+<table id="A1.Ex22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">
+
+<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
+<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

+<p id="Thmproposition3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where the Jensen penalty <math id="Thmproposition3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathfrak{J}_{\Gamma}(X,\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{X,\pi}\operatorname{KL}(P\|p_{\theta}(\cdot|\Gamma_{\pi}))-\mathbb{E}_{X}\operatorname{KL}(P\|\bar{p}_{\theta})\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔍</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></msub><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>X</mi></msub><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{J}_{\Gamma}(X,\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{X,\pi}\operatorname{KL}(P\|p_{\theta}(\cdot|\Gamma_{\pi}))-\mathbb{E}_{X}\operatorname{KL}(P\|\bar{p}_{\theta})\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

+<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>A.4 EDFL and Corollary</h3>

+<div id="A1.SS4.2" class="ltx_proof">
+<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 5 (Expectation-level Decompression Law (EDFL)). ‣ 3.4 The Expectation-level Decompression Law ‣ 3 Theory: Order-Sensitive Information-Theoretic Guarantees ‣ Predictable Compression Failures Why Language Models Actually Hallucinate" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</h6>
+<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
+<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Convexity of <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Q\mapsto\operatorname{KL}(P\|Q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q\mapsto\operatorname{KL}(P\|Q)</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\operatorname{KL}(P\|S_{\pi})\geq\operatorname{KL}(P\|\mathbb{E}_{\pi}S_{\pi})=\operatorname{KL}(P\|\bar{S})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>S</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\operatorname{KL}(P\|S_{\pi})\geq\operatorname{KL}(P\|\mathbb{E}_{\pi}S_{\pi})=\operatorname{KL}(P\|\bar{S})</annotation></semantics></math>. For the Bernoulli bound, apply data processing to <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g:\mathcal{Y}\to\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g:\mathcal{Y}\to\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="g(y)=\mathbbm{1}_{\{y\in\mathcal{A}\}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mn>𝟙</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(y)=\mathbbm{1}_{\{y\in\mathcal{A}\}}</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\operatorname{KL}(P\|\bar{S})\geq\operatorname{KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(p)\|\operatorname{Ber}(\bar{q}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>S</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Ber</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>Ber</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{KL}(P\|\bar{S})\geq\operatorname{KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(p)\|\operatorname{Ber}(\bar{q}))</annotation></semantics></math>. Equality holds iff <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is sufficient for distinguishing <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>S</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{S}</annotation></semantics></math>.
+∎</span></p>
